facts.fact: Libya's Customs Authority announced on 21 August 2025 the full launch of the ASYCUDA customs system early the following month, after a two-week expert visit for the Customs Procedures Automation Project reviewed infrastructure readiness and implementation progress.
The IMF METAC says its August-September 2024 mission helped Libya Customs develop a National Standard Operating Procedure documenting the new automated clearing process using ASYCUDA World.
Libya Herald reports the Customs Authority approved a pilot of an electronic customs declaration portal at Ras Jadir and the Khoms sea port, as a first phase to computerise all ports.

An IMF METAC review says an ASYCUDA World 4.3.3 prototype is piloted only at the Port of Tripoli, used inconsistently for IM4 import declarations (four registered in May 2022, twelve in April) and not the primary declaration system.

facts.fact: The UN Global Survey 2025 records e-submission of customs declarations in Libya as not implemented, and the automated customs system and e-single window as at the planning stage.

Libya Herald reports that the Libyan Export Development Authority inaugurated its Unified Export Window (Single Window Export System) at the Ras Ajdir crossing with Tunisia on 21 January 2026, with customs directors present, for exporters' applications and completion of export procedures.

note: The system is import preregistration and cargo tracking at Al-Khoms, not customs declaration processing or a single window.
